description: SCIENCE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES: ONE OF THE MOST IMPORTANT FINDINGS MADE BY PARKER SOLAR PROBE (PSP) IS THE LARGE NUMBER OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS (SWITCHBACKS FOR SHORT) IN THE NEAR-SUN SPACE. SWITCHBACKS  WITH TYPICAL TIME SCALES OF MINUTES TO TENS OF MINUTES  ARE LOCAL POLARITY-REVERSALS OF THE (RADIAL) MAGNETIC FIELD AND ARE TYPICALLY HIGHLY ALFV NIC  WITH CORRELATIONS BETWEEN VELOCITY AND MAGNETIC FIELD CORRESPONDING TO LARGE-AMPLITUDE OUTWARD-PROPAGATING ALFV N WAVES. MANY OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES SUGGEST THAT SWITCHBACKS PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE EVOLUTION OF SOLAR WIND. EVIDENCE OF MAGNETIC RECONNECTION AND WAVE ACTIVITIES WAS FOUND AT THE BOUNDARIES OF SWITCHBACKS  AND THESE PROCESSES MAY FACILITATE THE ENERGY DISSIPATION IN THE SWITCHBACKS. SIMULATIONS SHOW THAT THE SWITCHBACKS CAN BE DESTROYED BY PARAMETRIC DECAY  RELEASING ENERGY TO THE BACKGROUND PLASMA. THUS  SWITCHBACKS MAY CONTRIBUTE SIGNIFICANTLY TO THE HEATING AND ACCELERATION OF THE SOLAR WIND. HOWEVER  HOW AND WHERE THE SWITCHBACKS ARE GENERATED IS STILL A MYSTERY  AND A QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS OF THEIR INFLUENCES ON THE BACKGROUND SOLAR WIND IS STILL NEEDED. THE APPEARANCE AND AMPLITUDE OF SWITCHBACKS ARE USUALLY MODULATED BY A LARGE TIME SCALE  TYPICALLY SEVERAL HOURS  SO THAT THE SWITCHBACKS APPEAR IN PATCHES. THESE PATCHES ARE BELIEVED TO BE REMNANTS OF SPATIAL AND/OR TEMPORAL EFFECTS IN THE CORONAL SOURCE REGION OF THE WIND  SO THAT STUDYING THE PATCHES MAY HELP TO UNDERSTAND THE ORIGINS OF SWITCHBACKS. THUS  WE PROPOSE TO ANALYZE IN-SITU SATELLITE MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE-SENSING OBSERVATIONS OF THE SUN IN ORDER TO ANSWER THE FOLLOWING QUESTIONS: (1) HOW DO THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS EVOLVE IN THE SOLAR WIND? WHAT CAN WE LEARN ABOUT THE GENERATION MECHANISMS OF THE SWITCHBACKS FROM THEIR PROPERTIES? (2) HOW MUCH DO THE SWITCHBACKS CONTRIBUTE TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND? (3) WHAT IS THE ORIGIN OF THE SWITCHBACK PATCHES? ARE THEY RELATED TO CERTAIN SPATIAL STRUCTURES OR TEMPORAL PROCESSES IN THE SOLAR CORONA? METHODOLOGY: WE WILL COMBINE IN-SITU MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND REMOTE SENSING MEASUREMENTS OF THE SOLAR ATMOSPHERE. WE WILL USE INSITU DATA FROM PSP  SOLAR ORBITER AND WIND TO IDENTIFY SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES IN THE SOLAR WIND. THEN WE WILL CONDUCT ANALYSES OF THE PROPERTIES OF SWITCHBACKS AND SWITCHBACK PATCHES  INCLUDING HOW THEY EVOLVE AS THE SOLAR WIND PROPAGATES. WE WILL SELECT TIME INTERVALS WHEN PSP IS GOING THROUGH FAST RADIAL SCAN AND ESTIMATE THE CONTRIBUTION OF THE SWITCHBACKS TO THE ACCELERATION AND HEATING OF THE SOLAR WIND. THE REMOTE SENSING DATA WILL BE FROM HELIOSEISMIC AND MAGNETIC IMAGER (HMI) AND ATMOSPHERIC IMAGING ASSEMBLY (AIA) ONBOARD SOLAR DYNAMICS OBSERVATORY (SDO). WE WILL USE THE REMOTE SENSING DATA  COMBINED WITH TECHNIQUES SUCH AS THE POTENTIAL-FIELD-SOURCE-SURFACE MODEL  TO IDENTIFY SOURCE REGIONS OF THE SOLAR WIND STREAMS MEASURED IN-SITU BY PSP AND OTHER SATELLITES. RELEVANCE: KNOWLEDGE OF THE PROPERTIES AND ORIGINS OF MAGNETIC SWITCHBACKS WILL GREATLY IMPROVE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ORIGINS OF THE SOLAR WIND AND HOW THE SOLAR WIND IS ACCELERATED AND HEATED. description: WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE GRAIN MIGRATION IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK DURING THE ERA OF CHONDRULE FORMATION BY INVESTIGATING THE CHEMICAL AND O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS. WHILE THE DISCOVERY OF CALCIUM-ALUMINUM RICH INCLUSIONS AND CHONDRULE-LIKE OBJECTS IN COMET WILD 2 SHOWED THAT OUTWARD MIGRATION OF SUB-MM SIZED-PARTICLES OCCURRED VERY EARLY IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM  THE EXTENT AND DIRECTION(S) OF MIGRATION AFTER THIS EARLY TIME IN SOLAR SYSTEM HISTORY IS NOT KNOWN. THE PROPOSED WORK IS RELEVANT TO THE SCOPE OF THE EMERGING WORLDS PROGRAM  AS ITS GOAL IS   TO ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE OF THE SOLAR SYSTEM BY INVESTIGATING HOW IT FORMED AND EVOLVED  THROUGH THE ANALYSES OF EXTRATERRESTRIAL MATERIALS IN THE LABORATORY. EMERGING WORLDS IS MOST APPROPRIATE FOR THIS RESEARCH SINCE IT IS RELEVANT TO MULTIPLE TOPICS LISTED IN THE PROGRAM S SCOPE IN C.2.  INCLUDING  BUT NOT LIMITED TO:  STUDIES OF ALL ASPECTS OF MATERIALS PRESENT AND PROCESSES OCCURRING IN AND AFFECTING THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  . WE WILL ACHIEVE THESE GOALS BY DETERMINING THE MORPHOLOGIES  ELEMENTAL  AND O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS USING STATE-OF-THE-ART COORDINATED MICROANALYTICAL TECHNIQUES (FIELD EMISSION ELECTRON PROBE MICROANALYSIS AND SECONDARY ION MASS SPECTROMETRY). PARTIALLY MELTED CHONDRULES CONTAIN UNMELTED CHONDRULE PRECURSOR SILICATES THAT SURVIVED HEATING DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION  WHICH ARE TERMED RELICT GRAINS. THESE RELICT GRAINS MAY BE PRIMORDIAL SILICATES RELATED TO REFRACTORY INCLUSIONS  RECYCLED CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS FROM THE SAME METEORITE GROUP  XENOCRYSTS FROM ANOTHER CHONDRITE GROUP  OR DEBRIS FROM DIFFERENTIATED/ UNDIFFERENTIATED PLANETESIMALS. CHONDRULES FROM DISTINCT METEORITE GROUPS HAVE CHARACTERISTIC CHEMICAL AND/OR O-ISOTOPE COMPOSITIONS  ALLOWING US TO IDENTIFY THE ORIGIN(S) OF RELICT GRAINS. RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES ARE IMPORTANT TO STUDY BECAUSE WE KNOW THEY WERE PRESENT DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM. BY CONSTRAINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF RELICT GRAINS IN CHONDRULES FROM METEORITE GROUPS WITH DISTINCT ESTABLISHED FORMATION AGES THAT FORMED AT DISTINCT RADIAL LOCATIONS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK  WE WILL INVESTIGATE GRAIN MIGRATION BETWEEN CHONDRITE GROUPS PRIOR TO AND DURING CHONDRULE FORMATION AND CONSTRAIN THEIR SOURCE(S). OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT CHONDRULE FRAGMENTS MIGRATED BETWEEN DISTINCT CHONDRULE-FORMING REGIONS  FROM THE NON-CARBONACEOUS [NC] METEORITE REGION IN THE INNER SOLAR SYSTEM TO THE CARBONACEOUS CHONDRITE [CC] METEORITE REGION IN THE OUTER SOLAR SYSTEM REGION  IMPLYING OUTWARD MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK. OUR DATA WILL HAVE SIGNIFICANT IMPLICATIONS FOR MIXING OF MATERIAL IN THE EARLY SOLAR SYSTEM  AND ASSUMING 26AL HOMOGENEITY  PROVIDE ESTIMATES ON THE TIMING OF SUCH MIGRATION(S) BETWEEN FORMATION REGIONS. DETERMINING THE ORIGIN(S) OF CHONDRULE PRECURSORS  RELICT GRAINS  WILL PROVIDE ANALYTICAL CONSTRAINTS TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT THE RADIAL MIGRATION OF GRAINS IN THE PROTOPLANETARY DISK DURING THE ERA OF CHONDRULE FORMATION WAS OUTWARD.

MEETING THIS OBJECTIVE REQUIRES THE ABILITY TO MEASURE SNOW ALBEDO AND UNDERSTAND HOW AND WHY IT VARIES  ESPECIALLY IN THE WORLD'S MOUNTAINS  WHICH COMPRISE A QUARTER OF THE WORLD'S LAND AREA BUT PRODUCE AT LEAST HALF OF THE RUNOFF. THE EUROPEAN SPACE AGENCY HAS SELECTED A CANDIDATE SENSOR TO ADDRESS THESE NEEDS. THE COPERNICUS HYPERSPECTRAL IMAGING MISSION FOR THE ENVIRONMENT (CHIME) IS IN PHASE B1  WITH SPATIAL RESOLUTION OF 20 TO 30 M  SPECTRAL COVERAGE FROM 400 TO 2500 NM AT RESOLUTION OF 10 NM OR LESS  REVISIT INTERVAL OF 10 TO 12 DAYS  10:30 EQUATOR CROSSING TIME  LAUNCH 2026. EXPERIENCE AND CROSS-VALIDATION WOULD BENEFIT THE DEVELOPMENT OF NASA S SURFACE BIOLOGY AND GEOLOGY DESIGNATED OBSERVABLE AND SHORTEN THE REVISIT INTERVAL. Q1. HOW DOES SENSITIVITY OF IMAGING SPECTROSCOPY RETRIEVALS OF SNOW AND GLACIER PROPERTIES IN THE MOUNTAINS VARY DEPENDING ON THE SOLUTION METHOD FOR THE INVERSION AND THE ATMOSPHERIC CORRECTION? Q2. HOW CAN A FUSION OF SPECTROSCOPY DATA WITH MORE FREQUENT AND BROADER COVERAGE FROM MULTISPECTRAL SENSORS ENABLE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE SNOW AND ICE PROPERTIES AND RADIATIVE FORCING OVER LARGER AREAS AND ACROSS SEASONS AND YEARS? USE CHIME S SURFACE REFLECTANCE PRODUCTS  CORRECTED FOR TOPOGRAPHY  TO INVERT THE SIGNAL FOR RETRIEVAL OF SNOW PROPERTIES  AND THEREBY INFORM ESA OF FEASIBLE LEVEL 2 PRODUCTS FOR SNOW AND GLACIER PROPERTIES. PRE-LAUNCH ANALYZE SPATIAL VARIABILITY OF SNOW SPECIFIC SURFACE AREA  RADIATIVE FORCING BY DUST  CARBON  AND ORGANIC MATERIAL  AND RESULTING SNOW AND ICE ALBEDO USING AVAILABLE DATA FROM AIRBORNE SPECTROMETERS. POST-LAUNCH PLAN SIMILAR ANALYSES GLOBALLY IN REPRESENTATIVE MOUNTAIN RANGES. O3. IN MOST SNOW-DOMINATED ENVIRONMENTS  NET SOLAR RADIATION DRIVES MELT AND METAMORPHISM OF SNOW. IN MODELING THESE PROCESSES  INACCURACY IN THE ESTIMATION OF SNOW ALBEDO CONSTITUTES THE MAJOR SOURCE OF UNCERTAINTY IN CALCULATING THE SNOWPACK S ENERGY BALANCE. TRANSBOUNDARY POLLUTION IS A MAJOR CONCERN IN THE REGION  AS HIGH EMISSIONS FROM REGIONAL SOURCES SUCH AS FIRES CAN LEAD TO COMPLEX INFLUENCES ON LOCAL AQ. THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO BUILD A FULLY CUSTOMIZED AND SUSTAINABLE AQ TOOLKIT FOR ADVANCING AQ MONITORING  FORECASTING  AND MANAGEMENT DECISIONS IN THE HKH FOCUS COUNTRIES. OUR ML ALGORITHMS WILL UTILIZE SPECTRAL  SPATIAL  AND TEMPORAL INFORMATION FROM DIFFERENT BAND COMBINATIONS ON NEW-GENERATION GEOSTATIONARY SATELLITE SENSORS TO ACCURATELY CLASSIFY DUST AND SMOKE IN THE HKH REGION. THE AOD AND FIRE DETECTION PRODUCTS WILL BE USED AS INPUT INTO A HIGH-RESOLUTION WEATHER RESEARCH AND FORECASTING MODEL WITH CHEMISTRY (WRF-CHEM) CONFIGURATION OVER THE REGION. THE OPERATIONAL WRF-CHEM MODEL WILL ALSO BE UPDATED WITH A NEW ANTHROPOGENIC EMISSIONS INVENTORY BASED ON A SATELLITE-BASED ADJUSTMENT METHOD. LASTLY  THE FIRE DETECTION LOCATIONS  DUST CLASSIFICATIONS  AND AEROSOL LAYER HEIGHT PRODUCTS WILL BE USED TO INITIALIZE AN AUTOMATED HYSPLIT DISPERSION FORECASTING SYSTEM OVER HKH FOR RAPIDLY WARNING THE PUBLIC OF AQ EXCEEDANCES RELATED TO DUST AND SMOKE EPISODES. description: CLAY MINERALS PRESENT A CONUNDRUM ON MARS- WHILE WE OBSERVE RELATIVELY THICK LAYERS OF CLAY MINERALS AND OTHER SECONDARY MINERALS WHICH ARE TYPICALLY FORMED THROUGH AQUEOUS PROCESSES ON EARTH  CLIMATE MODELS PREDICT COLD CONDITIONS ON EARLY MARS THAT PRECLUDE LONG-TERM STABILITY OF FRESH WATER ON THE SURFACE. ADDING SALT DECREASES THE FREEZING POINT OF WATER  ALLOWING LONG-TERM STABILITY OF LIQUID WATER AT COLDER TEMPERATURES AND LOWER PRESSURES. SALTS ALSO ALLOW FOR THIN FILMS OF WATER AT MINERAL SURFACES. PREVIOUS EXPERIMENTS CONDUCTED BY OUR RESEARCH GROUP DEMONSTRATE THAT MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS CAN PRODUCE CLAY MINERALS WITHIN WEEKS OF REACTION WITH PRIMARY ROCK-FORMING SILICATES. HERE WE AIM TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE THE MINERALOGY AND ABUNDANCE OF CLAY MINERAL PHASES PRODUCED WHEN PRIMARY SILICATE MINERALS REACT WITH HIGH SALINITY BRINES. IN ADDITION  WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE CLAY ALTERATION IN HIGH SALINITY BRINES TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND THE POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF EVAPORATING/FREEZING SURFACE WATERS AS WELL AS HIGH DENSITY DIAGENETIC FLUIDS ON CLAY MINERALOGY AND CHEMISTRY. OUR PREVIOUS MINERAL-BRINE DISSOLUTION EXPERIMENTS WERE DESIGNED TO MEASURE PRIMARY MINERAL WEATHERING RATES IN HIGH SALINITY FLUIDS. WHILE SECONDARY CLAY MINERALS WERE OBSERVED AT THE MICRON SCALE VIA SCANNING ELECTRON MICROSCOPY (SEM) AND RAMAN SPECTROSCOPY  THEY PROVED DIFFICULT TO FULLY ANALYZE USING X-RAY DIFFRACTION (XRD) METHODS DUE TO THEIR LIMITED ABUNDANCE. FURTHERMORE  WE WILL EXPLORE THE ROLE OF BRINE CHEMISTRY ON CLAY DIAGENESIS AND WEATHERING BY REACTING CLAY MINERALS WITH THE BRINES. MINERAL AND ROCK SAMPLES WILL BE REACTED WITH NEAR-SATURATED BRINES AND 1:10 DILUTED SOLUTIONS OF NACL  NA2SO4  NACLO4  CACL2  MGCL2  MGSO4  AND NH4CL OVER 6 MONTHS  THEN FILTERED TO COLLECT THE SOLID AND LIQUID REACTION PRODUCTS. ADDITIONAL HIGH TEMPERATURE (350K FOR 50 DAYS) AND LOW TEMPERATURE EXPERIMENTS (250K FOR 450 DAYS) WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH BASALT AND MAFIC GLASS. THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE SEPARATED VIA WET SIEVING AND CENTRIFUGE TECHNIQUES. SIMILAR EXPERIMENTS WILL ALSO BE CONDUCTED USING CLAY STANDARDS (KAOLINITE  NONTRONITE  SMECTITE  CHLORITE). BULK CHEMISTRY OF THE CLAY-SIZED FRACTION WILL BE DETERMINED VIA ICP OPTICAL EMISSION SPECTROSCOPY ANALYSIS OF DIGESTIONS. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE REACTION PRODUCT MINERALOGY  MORPHOLOGY  CHEMISTRY AND TEXTURAL RELATIONSHIPS USING BOTH SCANNING AND TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF POTENTIAL MINERAL-BRINE INTERACTIONS ON MARS AND OTHER SALTY WORLDS  INCLUDING CERES  EUROPA  AND ENCELADUS AND WILL PROVIDE RICHER CONTEXT FOR INTERPRETING MINERAL ASSEMBLAGES AND SEDIMENTARY ROCKS  INCLUDING CLAY MINERALS  OBSERVED ON THESE BODIES. description: MOROCCO IS A DROUGHT-PRONE  CLIMATE-CONSTRAINED COUNTRY THAT HAS MADE SIGNIFICANT INVESTMENTS IN AGRICULTURE WITH THE GOAL OF ENHANCING THE ADOPTION OF HIGHER-VALUE CROPPING SYSTEMS FOR ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. THE MOROCCAN GOVERNMENT CURRENTLY OFFERS A MULTI-PERIL INSURANCE PROGRAM FOR CEREAL CROPS BUT HAS NOT YET DEVELOPED A PRODUCT THAT COULD HELP ABSORB THE RISKS IMPEDING THE ADOPTION OF SUCH HIGHER VALUE  BUT RISKIER  CROPPING SYSTEMS. WITHIN THIS CONTEXT  TWO EARLY-CAREER SCIENTISTS WITH SPECIALTIES IN SPATIAL AND ECONOMIC ANALYSIS  RESPECTIVELY  WILL LEAD A PROJECT TO EVALUATE THE POSSIBILITY OF USING REMOTELY-SENSED INDICATORS TO EFFECTIVELY SHIELD FARMERS FROM RISKS OF ADOPTING HIGHER VALUE CROPS VIA THEIR USE IN AN INDEXED INSURANCE AND/OR DROUGHT RELIEF PROGRAM. ACHIEVING THIS OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE WILL INVOLVE THREE MAIN TASKS: 1. DETECTING THE EXTENT OF OLIVE CROPPING SYSTEMS AND EVALUATING THE DEGREE OF CONVERSION FROM CEREAL CROPS TO OLIVES. 2. EVALUATING SOCIOECONOMIC CONDITIONS AND RISK MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES IN TWO STUDY AREAS OF MOROCCO. THIS STEP WILL FIRST INVOLVE EXPERT ELICITATION TO GROUND THE ANALYSIS IN THE REALITIES AND PERCEIVED RISKS IN THE SUPPLY CHAIN  AND WILL BE FOLLOWED BY A SERIES OF STRATIFIED SURVEYS AMONG AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS IN TWO OLIVE PRODUCING REGIONS OF MOROCCO WHOSE AGRO-CLIMATIC CONDITIONS VARY. 3. PERENNIAL CROPS ARE EMBLEMATIC OF THE POSSIBILITY TO ADOPT HIGHER VALUE CROPPING SYSTEMS THAT ARE OTHERWISE TOO RISKY FOR MANY FARMERS TO TAKE ON WITHOUT INSURANCE. EVEN IF THEY ARE DROUGHT-RESISTANT  PERENNIALS ARE MUCH MORE COSTLY THAN MANY ANNUAL CROPS AND INVOLVE A LONG PERIOD BEFORE THEY HAVE ECONOMICALLY-HARVESTABLE FRUITS. EVEN ONCE PRODUCING  WEATHER FLUCTUATION REMAINS A RISK: RECENT REPORTS SUGGEST MOROCCAN OLIVE FARMERS PERCEIVED YIELD DECLINES ON THE ORDER OF 36-64% LESS THAN EXPECTED IN RECENT DRY YEARS. DROUGHT CAN THEREFORE AMPLIFY RISK EXPOSURE FOR FARMERS WHEN THE FARMERS FACE HIGHER ABSOLUTE LOSSES RELATIVE TO THEIR POTENTIAL. DESPITE THE IMPORTANCE OF PERENNIALS  MOST STUDIES EVALUATING INDEXED PRODUCTS FOR AGRICULTURE FOCUS ON ANNUAL CROPPING SYSTEMS OR BROAD INDICATORS OF DROUGHT STRESS RATHER THAN THE PARTICULARS OF HIGH VALUE  LONG-TERM INVESTMENTS. OUR INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH TO INTEGRATING SOCIAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL PROCESSES AS WELL AS DISAGGREGATING IMPACTS ACROSS SPACE ALIGNS WITH THE LCLUC RESEARCH PRIORITIES TO UNDERSTAND THE SUSTAINABILITY  VULNERABILITY  AND RESILIENCE OF HUMAN LAND USE. description: DETECTION OF OVER 4700 EXOPLANETS SUGGESTS THAT CLOSE-IN  ROCKY EXOPLANETS OF MAGNETICALLY ACTIVE G  K AND M DWARFS SHOULD BE EXPOSED TO HIGH STELLAR CORONAL X-RAY AND EXTREME ULTRAVIOLET (XUV) AND LARGE STELLAR WIND MASS FLUXES. THE KEPLER AND TESS MISSIONS HAVE REVEALED FREQUENT SUPERFLARES ON COOL G--M PLANET-HOSTING DWARF STARS  PROVIDING A MECHANISM BY WHICH HOST STARS COULD DIRECTLY INFLUENCE THE PHYSICAL AND CHEMICAL EVOLUTION OF EXOPLANETARY ATMOSPHERES. SOLAR STUDIES SUGGEST THAT LARGE FLARES ARE ACCOMPANIED BY THE ERUPTION OF MAGNETIZED CORONAL PLASMA REFERRED TO AS CORONAL MASS EJECTIONS (CMES). WHILE STELLAR SUPERFLARES CAN BE DIRECTLY DETECTED AND CHARACTERIZED IN XUV  OPTICAL  AND RADIO WAVELENGTHS  THE SIGNATURES OF STELLAR WINDS AND SUPERFLARE CMES REMAIN ELUSIVE AND REQUIRE DETAILED THEORETICAL MODELING. OUR MAJOR SCIENCE QUESTIONS ARE: 1.) WHAT ARE THE CORONAL XUV EMISSION AND STELLAR WIND MASS FLUXES FROM ACTIVE G--M DWARFS? 2.) HOW DOES THE EVOLUTION OF THE MAGNETIC FIELD AND STELLAR ATMOSPHERE TRIGGER STELLAR SUPERFLARES? WHAT IS THE NATURE OF THE STELLAR FLARE--CME RELATIONSHIP AND WHAT ARE THEIR OBSERVATIONAL SIGNATURES? 3.) HOW ARE EXOPLANETARY SPACE WEATHER IMPACTS DRIVEN BY THE HOST STAR'S XUV EMISSION  AMBIENT STELLAR WINDS  SUPERFLARES AND THEIR ASSOCIATED CMES AND ENERGETIC PARTICLE FLUXES? THE SCIENCE GOALS OF THE PROPOSED INTERDISCIPLINARY STUDY ARE TO USE AVAILABLE HST  XMM-NEWTON  TESS  NICER AND SPECTROPOLARIMETRIC OBSERVATIONS OF ACTIVE G--M DWARFS AS INPUTS AND CONSTRAINTS FOR MULTI-DIMENSIONAL MAGNETOHYDRODYNAMIC (MHD) MODELING OF (A) THE STRUCTURE AND ENERGIZATION OF THE MAGNETIC FIELD CONFIGURATIONS OF STARSPOT GROUPS/STELLAR ACTIVE REGIONS  AND (B) THE RAPID RELEASE OF FREE MAGNETIC ENERGY DURING STELLAR SUPERFLARES AND THE DYNAMICS AND OBSERVATIONAL SIGNATURES OF THEIR ASSOCIATED CMES. THE PROPOSED INVESTIGATION IS HIGHLY RELEVANT TO XRP PROGRAMMATIC QUESTIONS AS IT CROSSES NASA S MULTI-DIVISIONAL BOUNDARIES THROUGH THE COUPLING OF DATA OBTAINED WITH FLAGSHIP ASTROPHYSICS MISSIONS WITH HELIOPHYSICS MODELS TO ADDRESS THE PROGRAM S GOAL: "OBSERVATIONAL CHARACTERIZATION OF EXOPLANETS  THEIR ATMOSPHERES  THEIR INTERACTIONS WITH THEIR HOST STARS  OR SPECIFIC HOST STAR PROPERTIES THAT DIRECTLY IMPACT OUR UNDERSTANDING OF EXOPLANETARY SYSTEMS." THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL HAVE A POTENTIALLY TRANSFORMATIVE IMPACT ON THE FIELD OF EXOPLANET RESEARCH BECAUSE IT EXPANDS THE DEFINITION OF HABITABLE ZONES EXPOSED TO STELLAR IONIZING RADIATION AND PROVIDES CRITICAL INPUTS FOR MODELING AND CHARACTERIZATION OF EXOPLANET ATMOSPHERES AND THEIR EVOLUTION. THIS PROJECT IS DIRECTLY RELEVANT TO DATA FROM HST  KEPLER AND TESS AND WILL LEAD TO PREDICTIONS THAT CAN BE TESTED WITH OBSERVATIONS.
